content.title: Accessing a Secure Email Message
content.summary: Email encryption enhances security by ensuring that sensitive data remains unreadable to unauthorized parties, thus aiding in regulatory compliance and mitigating the impact of data breaches. Recipients of secure messages must register with Proofpoint Encryption to access their messages, and once logged in, they can read and respond to messages according to their organization's security policies. Options for responding include Reply, Reply All, and Forward, with varying capabilities for adding recipients based on security restrictions.
content.body:
## Background and Key Benefits of Email Encryption

- **Enhanced security:** Encryption adds a critical layer of protection, ensuring that data remains unreadable even if another security measure fails. This is especially important when communicating over the Internet.
- **Regulatory compliance:**Many regulations, including (but not limited to) GDPR and HIPAA, require strong data protection measures. Encryption helps organizations meet these compliance mandates by ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of personal and sensitive information.
- **Protection against breaches:**If a data breach occurs on any side (sender, platform, or recipient), data remains secure because it is unusable without the decryption key. This can significantly reduce the impact of a breach.
- **Mitigation of risk:**By preventing unauthorized access, encryption adds diligence and preventative measures to assure privacy and confidentiality in the event of a data breach or unauthorized intercept, including accidental or incidental exposure.
- **Maintains data integrity:**Encryption helps ensure that the data has not been tampered with during storage or transmission. By keeping data unreadable (at rest, without the key), it maintains its reliability.
- **Ensures privacy:** Encryption is a core component of data privacy, especially in a digital world where information is shared across different networks. It prevents sensitive information from being shared with unintended third parties.

## Recipients: Accessing the Secure Messages

When you receive a secure message, it will look like this in your mailbox:

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6707)

Message informing you that this is a secure message with a link to read the message and an expiration date.

### Registering with Proofpoint Encryption

The first time you receive a secure message, you will be prompted to create an account to register with Proofpoint Encryption.

You will see the following message the first time you use Proofpoint Encryption and also when you initiate a secure message:

**First time here?** You’ll be asked to register.

**Already registered?** You’ll be asked to log in.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6698)

Message with input box for email address.

You might be required to create an account that includes a security question in addition to the password.

This is the registration that requires a security question:![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6713)

Dialog with inputs for first name, last name, password, password confirmation, and security question

This is the registration that does not include a security question:![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6712)

Dialog box with inputs for first name, last name, password, and password confirmation

Fill in the fields, select and answer a security question if applicable, and the click "Continue."

**Note:** Your password cannot contain spaces.

### Reading and Responding to the Message

After registration or logging in, you will be able to read the message. If your organization's security policy allows, you will have the options to **Reply**, **Reply All**, **Forward** or **Save As**. You will see a button for the available options.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6708)

Email window showing buttons for Reply, Reply All, Forward, Save As...

Each button will give you different results:

Clicking "Reply" will not allow you to add more recipients to the message:

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6709)

Email window without the ability to add recipients

Clicking "Reply All" will allow you to add more recipients to the message:

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6710)

Email window with the ability to add recipients using the CC line

If you click "Forward" you can add recipients to the message. The recipients might be restricted to certain domains, according to the City's security policies:

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6700)

Email window showing the ability to forward an encrypted email

Use the "Save As" button to download your secure message to your computer. You will have options as to how you want to save the message:

- Save Message Body as HTML: this will download the message body and name the file <message subject>.html
- Save as Zip Archive: this will download the message and associated attachments and name the file <message subject>.zip
- Save as EML Message: this will compose a RFC2822 message based upon the Secure Reader Message Content. This will not include embedded images.

**Note:** Once the email is downloaded in any form, the downloaded file or files will no longer be encrypted by Proofpoint.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6705)

Decrypted email window with the options for saving the message to your computer

Click "Logout" when you are done with the message.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6703)

The "Logout" button at the top of the right side of the screen is highlighted

The next time you need to read a secure message, you will be prompted to log in to Proofpoint Encryption again, using your email address and password.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6704)

Proofpoint dialog box asking for a username and password

### Password Expired

Your password will expire after a period of time. The password expiration is determined by your email administrator. If your password is about to expire, you will see the message "Your password will expire in <number> days" displaced in a secure message.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6706)

Dialog box telling you that your password will expire

Click the link next to the expiration message to reset your password.

If your password expires before you have a chance to reset it, you will be prompted to reset it the next time you read a secure message.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6711)

Dialog box for changing your password

### Forgotten Password

If you have forgotten your password, you can click the "Forgot Password" link on the login screen.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6699)

Message highlighting the "Forgot Password" link in the dialog box

The password reset procedure depends upon how your Proofpoint Encryption account is set up.

- If you have a security question, you will be prompted to answer the question. You will then be prompted to reset your password.
- If you do not have a security question, you will receive an email message with a link in it. Click the link to reset your password.

### Decrypting Secure Messages from a Mobile Device

When you receive a secure message on a mobile device, it contains a link that you can click to decrypt the message and read it on your mobile device. The message is “clickable” typically for two days.

The next illustration shows how the secure message displays on a mobile device, depending upon how it is set up:

- If Secure Reader Proxy is Enabled
- If Secure Reader Proxy is Disabled
- If Decrypt Assist is enabled

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6697)

Message stating that this is a secure message and displaying the deadline to open it on mobile. In this case, Secure Reader Proxy is enabled or disabled, and Decrypt Assist is enabled.

Generally, after two days (or the number of days presently configured), you need to open the attachment that contains the Secure Reader Proxy email address to forward the secure message to the proxy. You will then receive another message with a URL to click to authenticate with Proofpoint Encryption. After authentication, you can read the secure message.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6697)

Message stating that this is a secure message and displaying the deadline to open it on mobile. In this case, Secure Reader Proxy is enabled, and Decrypt Assist is disabled.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6696)

Message stating that this is a secure message; to read it, open the attachment. In this case, Secure Reader Proxy is disabled, and Decrypt Assist is disabled

## Internal Users - Composing a Secure Message to External Users

When you want to send a secure message, all you need to do is use your regular email application and enter the word **[encrypt]** (including square brackets) into the **Subject** field of your message. Include the square brackets.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6702)

Email window showing the word "encrypt" in square brackets on the subject line
